solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Key item that's extremely reliable?

definitions.meaning: an ... piano is a musical instrument played by its keys
an honourable, thoroughly trustworthy person can be described this way

explanation.surface: Someone looking for the most dependable part of a lock or keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key item' looks like the most important thing, but it means something with keys: a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a person of strict honesty and integrity; as a noun it names the vertical piano with keys.

clue.text: Others supporting a French revolutionary state

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece goes underneath

parts.note: un is French for a
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Other people backing a French revolutionary regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitation and disturbance among a population, the condition of a society close to revolt.

clue.text: Embarrassed over merciful attitude shown by Cornish town

parts.note: embarrassed people go red
ruth is an old word for pity or compassion

explanation.surface: A flushed town in Cornwall showing compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' only joins the pieces, RED above RUTH in the down answer. Redruth is a former mining town in Cornwall, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Redruth is a town in west Cornwall once at the heart of the tin-mining industry.

clue.text: Daughter participates in sailings at sea, showing smooth actions

indicators.note: joins inside the rearranged letters
confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter takes part in voyages, displaying graceful movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' gives a rearrangement of SAILINGS, and 'participates in' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, these are continuous slides up or down between pitches, played as one smooth sweep.

clue.text: Suggestion about name precedes obsessively collecting English popular music production

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second
the advice word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: a tip is a suggestion or piece of advice

indicators.note: taking in, so the abbreviation goes inside the adverb

parts.note: anally means in an obsessively fussy way

explanation.surface: Advice on naming comes before the fussy gathering of English pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obsessively' is the adverb from the slang 'anal', meaning fussily over-meticulous. Tin Pan Alley was a street in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin Pan Alley was the New York songwriting and publishing district, standing for the commercial popular song industry.

clue.text: The relief of adopting atheism?

parts.note: an atheist has seen the end of God, read as ..., a welcome relief

explanation.surface: A sceptic sighs with relief at finally giving up belief in a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as GOD'S END: adopting atheism means God's existence comes to an end for you.
explanation.definitionFit: A welcome, unexpected piece of luck or help that brings relief is often called a gift from heaven.

clue.text: Vapour pressure forced from openings

indicators.note: driven out of, so the letter leaves the word

parts.note: gaps are openings
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Steam under pressure escapes through holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas is a substance in its airy, vapour-like state, filling any container.

clue.text: Hidden party limiting old Government repeatedly

indicators.note: enclosing, so the party word goes round the rest

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the abbreviation is used twice over

explanation.surface: A secret party restricting the old government again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'lie doggo' is British slang for hiding quietly and keeping still.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for out of sight and keeping quiet, as in the phrase lie low and stay still.

clue.text: Attention given to story run at a previous date

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention
a lie is a story, a falsehood
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone listened to a tale that ran some time ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Means before now or sooner in time, at some former moment.

clue.text: Deacon is transformed as bishop

definitions.note: the answer as a noun means the bishop of a diocese

indicators.note: changed in form, so the deacon's letters plus the little word after are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deacon is promoted and changed into a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' does double service in the surface but belongs to the fodder: DEACONIS has the eight letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it names the bishop in charge of a diocese, a church district.

clue.text: I'd star gen organised for these

definitions.note: points back to the stars mentioned in the wordplay; a plural noun

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are put into a new order, arranged differently

explanation.surface: An astronomer saying good star information would help spot certain objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gen' is British slang for information. The definition 'these' refers back to the kind of star the surface mentions.
explanation.definitionFit: Large, cool, highly luminous stars late in their life are classified by astronomers under this name.

clue.text: Actress seen in zero clothing? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: instead of zero being followed by the clothing, the clothing comes first and zero after

parts.note: garb means clothes or dress
the figure zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A film star appearing wearing nothing at all, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zero clothing' would put O before GARB; 'Quite the reverse' swaps the order of the two pieces, not their letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Poor areas having no power in recessions

indicators.note: signals that one letter is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: economic slumps are recessions
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Deprived districts left without electricity during economic downturns.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-down, overcrowded urban districts housing the poor are called this.

clue.text: 'Stick with it' taken on board by guy pursuing apparent love goddess

parts.note: ap. is a dictionary abbreviation for apparent

indicators.note: something taken on board is held inside, so these letters go within the word for a man

parts.note: a guy is a man: he
a rod is a stick
it taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told to persevere by a man chasing a seeming romantic deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick with it' looks like one piece of advice but is two pieces. 'apparent' is abbreviated as in dictionaries, AP.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek deity of love and beauty, the counterpart of the Roman Venus.

clue.text: What forestalls draughts from outdoors?

parts.note: draughts are draught beers from the pub rather than cold air, and making your own at home means you need not go out for them

explanation.surface: Asking what keeps cold air out of the house, like a draught excluder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draughts' suggests cold air through cracks; here it means beer on draught, bought outside the home in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Making beer in your own kitchen does away with buying pints from the pub.

clue.text: A panorama, with sight bewitched?

indicators.note: under a spell, so the letters are thrown into confusion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A wide view seen through enchanted eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a view seen by enchanted eyes is just such a shifting dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a bewildering sequence of dreamlike images, like an enchanted wide view.

clue.text: Diluted spirits with water introducing special silky stuff

indicators.note: bringing in, so the letter is placed within the drink

parts.note: grog is spirit, originally rum, diluted with water
rain is falling water

explanation.surface: Watered spirits with special water added, producing something silky.
explanation.definitionFit: Grosgrain is a heavy ribbed silk or rayon fabric, used for ribbons.

clue.text: Sailor is knocked over in storm, rough

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: the turned letters go inside the storm word

parts.note: to rave is to storm or rage

indicators.note: upended, so in a down answer the two letters are read upwards

explanation.surface: A seaman is upended in a rough storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' looks like a noun but is the verb rave, to rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harsh and scraping, like coarse sandpaper, can be described as rough to the touch.

clue.text: Wimpy type concealing large bra?

definitions.meaning: a feeble, timid or oversensitive person, usually a man
a garment worn over a big bra by an adult woman, read literally

explanation.surface: A weakling hiding a sizeable item of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British slang for a soft or cowardly man; the second reading takes it literally as a top covering a woman's bra.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mocking British idiom for a weak, oversensitive or cowardly man.

clue.text: Unimportant person in organisation picked up skills in small vehicles

indicators.note: lifted up, so in a down answer the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cog in the machine is a minor figure in an organisation
arts are skills or crafts

explanation.surface: A lowly employee learnt some techniques while driving tiny cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like 'learnt' but turns COG upwards to make GOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Small, low motor vehicles used for racing on tracks, often by children.

clue.text: Release for Israeli musician accused of murder

indicators.note: setting the letters free lets them fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A call to free an Israeli performer charged with killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Salieri, the Italian composer, was rumoured to have poisoned Mozart, as in Amadeus.

clue.text: Quantity of pressure on that one particle

parts.note: the bar is a unit of pressure
yon is an old or dialect word for that

explanation.surface: A measurement of force on some particular speck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yon' is an old or Scottish word for that one, over there.
explanation.definitionFit: A baryon is a heavy subatomic particle such as a proton or neutron.

clue.text: Discharge publicity about Spielberg film (exemplary item)

parts.note: an arc is an electrical discharge between two points

indicators.note: the publicity word goes round the film title

parts.note: hype is extravagant publicity
E.T. is the 1982 Steven Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A sparkling promotional campaign for a Spielberg blockbuster, the perfect example.
explanation.definitionFit: An original model or perfect typical example of something is its prototype or classic pattern.

clue.text: Belgian artist exhibited in Amiens originally

indicators.note: shown within, so the letters sit inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A Belgian painter whose work first went on show in Amiens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like an initial-letters signal but is just part of the run that holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: James Ensor was a Belgian painter famous for masks and crowds, an early Expressionist.

clue.text: Festival enshrining British emperor

indicators.note: holding inside as in a shrine, so the abbreviation goes within the celebration word

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration

explanation.surface: A celebration that honours a British ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Servius Sulpicius Galba was a Roman ruler who reigned briefly in AD 68-69.

clue.text: Doctor is attending one Welshman

indicators.note: being beside or accompanying, so the numeral sits next to the doctor's letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A physician treating a single patient from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attending' just joins the pieces; in the surface it suggests a doctor caring for a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Idris is a traditional Welsh male name, borne by the legendary giant of Cader Idris.

clue.text: In Chancery (novel) offering no new legal tricks

indicators.note: new and unusual, so the letters are rearranged into a fresh order
the rearrangement is short of one letter, given by the next word

explanation.surface: A Dickensian-sounding tale of lawyers' sharp practice in the Court of Chancery.
explanation.walkthrough: '(novel)' looks like a book title note, recalling Dickens's Bleak House, but signals the rearrangement of IN CHANCERY with one N taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means trickery or sharp practice, used especially of lawyers' deceptive manoeuvres.

clue.text: Line would be included in this hint here

indicators.note: the answer is short of a letter: put it inside and you would have the thing you are reading, so take it away

parts.note: what you are reading right here is a crossword clue

explanation.surface: A self-referring remark that one more line would complete this hint.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: add L to the answer and you get the word for what is here, a CLUE. So remove L from CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a signal or prompt, a hint telling someone when to act or speak.

clue.text: Studio the French backed by the way? Not entirely

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the French article is read from right to left

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: the word for road loses its final letter

parts.note: a street is a way or road

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a studio is down a French road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns LE into EL; 'Not entirely' trims the last letter from STREET. ELSTREE is a famous film studio site north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Elstree in Hertfordshire is home to well-known film and television studios.

clue.text: Man, fashionable, carrying a flower

parts.note: a gent is a man

indicators.note: holding something inside, so the letter sits within the fashion word

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: A stylish gentleman holding a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentians are mountain plants with striking blue trumpet-shaped blooms.
